questions.prompt: What does the temperature tau change in CLIP-style zero-shot classification?
options: The number of classes that the model can distinguish in the prompt set
The arg-max class, because the temperature rescales the logits unevenly
The embedding dimension of the image and text encoders
The sharpness of the probabilities, not which class has the highest score
questions.explanation: Dividing all cosines by tau preserves their order, so the label is unchanged, but the gaps and the confidence change.

questions.prompt: Image and text embeddings are unit vectors with cosines 0.9 (class A) and 0.8 (class B), tau = 0.1. What is P(A)? Give 3 decimals.
Two prompts for the same class give different predictions on one image. What is the sound response?
options: Conclude that the model is broken, since the prompts should not change a prediction.
Treat prompts as hyperparameters: choose or ensemble them on a validation split.
Pick whichever prompt gives the best accuracy on the test set, then report that number.
Lower the temperature to zero so that the prompt wording no longer matters at all.
questions.explanation: Selecting on the test set leaks; ensembling or validation-based selection is the standard fix.

questions.prompt: A test set has 90 images of class A and 10 of class B; the model always predicts A. What is its macro accuracy (mean per-class recall)?
questions.explanation: Recall A = 1, recall B = 0, mean 0.5 (accuracy would be 0.9).

questions.prompt: How many test images give a 95% normal-approximation half-width of 0.05 when p = 0.5? Round up to an integer.
34 of 40 held-out images are correct. Which statement is best supported?
options: The true accuracy is exactly 85%, because 34 of 40 is 0.85.
The true accuracy is plausibly anywhere from about 71% to 93%.
The model is better than any model that scores 80% on another set.
The model is certainly above 90%, since most images were right.

questions.prompt: A foundation model scores well on a public benchmark. Describe how you would test whether it transfers to your robot's camera, including baselines, metrics and a rejection rule.
rubric: Uses a held-out set from the robot's own cameras that was not used to choose prompts or heads.
Includes baselines (majority class, small supervised model) and per-class metrics with intervals.
States a rejection rule such as a lower bound below a required recall.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
